children.text: St Augustine Parish in Bantay, beside Vigan, is a shrine to Our Lady of Charity. The hilltop bell tower was damaged in the 2022 earthquake. Check access to the church and the tower separately for your visit.

Bantay Church is the parish church of Saint Augustine in the town of Bantay, Ilocos Sur. Its official name is the Parish of Saint Augustine of Hippo, and it is also called the Archdiocesan Shrine of Our Lady of Charity (Nuestra Señora de la Caridad). According to Wikipedia, the church was completed in 1590 and is an active parish of the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia. It is close to Vigan's old town and can be reached by tricycle or kalesa, so it fits naturally into a Vigan trip. Bantay is a small town of about 37,000 people (37,088 in the 2024 census and 37,118 in the 2020 PSA census), close to the Abra River and the foothills of the Caraballo Mountains. One explanation links the town's name to the Spanish-era belfry that watched for pirates, while another says it comes from the "mountain" that devotees of Mary regard as a sacred place.

Bantay is famous for two reasons. First, the church enshrines an image of the Virgin Mary venerated as Our Lady of Charity. Following a coronation decree of Pope Pius XII (dated August 3, 1955 in the document Wikipedia cites), on January 12, 1956 the Apostolic Nuncio, Cardinal Egidio Vagnozzi, performed the crowning and named her "Patroness of Ilocandia." That is why Bantay town descriptions sometimes call her the "Queen of Ilocandia." Second, a Spanish-era bell tower stands on the hill beside the church, one of the most striking sights around Vigan.

The bell tower (Bantay Tower) is said to have been built in 1590, one year before the church. The church building was heavily damaged in World War II, and reconstruction began in 1950. The Neo-Gothic façade you see today is said to combine old methods using bricks and mud with Romanesque-style elements, designed to look grand and Spanish-inspired. The tower overlooks pasture and the province of Abra from its hilltop, so in the old days it served as a lookout against pirates and enemies. This is why one explanation links the town's name Bantay to a word meaning "to guard." Five bells are said to hang at the top.

After the July 2022 Abra earthquake, provincial tourism authorities temporarily closed both the Bantay Bell Tower and the church. Church services and hilltop tower access can follow different arrangements. Ask Bantay tourism or the parish separately about the exterior path and the tower stairs.

blocks.title: The image of Our Lady of Charity

children.text: The church enshrines an image of Our Lady of Charity, who is said to have been proclaimed "Patroness of Ilocandia" at the 1956 coronation. Pilgrims come here regularly, so it is polite to be quiet during Mass.

The tower stands on a hill beside the church and stands out even from a distance. It is said to date from 1590 and is reported to be a declared National Cultural Treasure. Since the 2022 earthquake, getting close to it may be restricted. Wikipedia explains that the tower was a Spanish-era lookout against pirates.

The tower was used as a lookout to spot and warn of pirates and enemies, and in World War II it is said to have served as a post for watching enemy movements. Its position overlooking the foothills toward Abra explains why.

blocks.title: A Neo-Gothic façade of brick and mud

children.text: The church façade was built in the Neo-Gothic style mixed with Romanesque-style elements to look grand, and it is made of bricks and mud. It was heavily damaged in the war and rebuilt from 1950, so you can see traces of both the old building and its reconstruction.

Part of the bell tower collapsed in the magnitude 7.0 earthquake. Restoration news and accessible areas are changing, so check before your visit. Ruined walls outside the church are reportedly used as an outdoor chapel.

The town fiesta honors Saint Augustine. It was originally held on August 28, but Fr. Alfredo Verzosa, parish priest from 1912 to 1916, moved it to May 5 because of the weather. If you go in early May you may see the festival atmosphere, but confirm the schedule locally.

Wikipedia and PhilAtlas put Bantay about 1–1.5 km from Vigan (straight-line distance between town centers). It is a short tricycle ride from the old town, so it is easy to include in a half-day route.

blocks.title: Quirino Bridge and the Abra River

children.text: The town has the Quirino Bridge over the Abra River, with the Caraballo Mountains in the distance. After seeing the tower, look around the riverside and the bridge to get a feel for Bantay. Wikipedia also lists Caniao Peak in the Caraballo Mountains among the town's attractions. Ask locally about hiking.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: From Vigan's old town to Bantay Church

children.text: Have breakfast in Vigan's old town and take a tricycle to Bantay. Agree on the fare and waiting time first.
Look around the church exterior and façade, then go inside and spend a quiet moment in front of the image of Our Lady of Charity.
View the bell tower area from outside. Access may be restricted after the earthquake, so follow the signs.
See the ruined walls outside the church and the outdoor chapel, then take a light walk through the town's streets.
Return to Vigan and have Vigan empanada for lunch.
A church visit needs only
1–2 hours
. Refrain from taking photos during Mass.

items.title: One-day Vigan and Bantay route
items.subtitle: Combining the old town and the church

children.text: Visit Bantay Church and the bell tower area first.
Return to Vigan and eat empanada or sinanglao.
Walk Plaza Salcedo, the cathedral, Padre Burgos House and Calle Crisologo.
Finish by watching the dancing fountain at Plaza Salcedo.
Many buses to Manila run at night, so check the timetable first.
Allow about
8–10 hours
by coach from Manila to Vigan. Check the booking for the pickup terminal, such as Cubao.
The
official Viron Transit route listing
gives Manila–Vigan from
one way. Overnight buses can arrive early, so check transport to your accommodation or Bantay in advance.
Bantay is close to Vigan, so no separate long-distance trip is needed.
As of September 2023, Vigan's own airport reportedly had no scheduled flights. The nearest airport is Laoag International Airport (LAO), about
1 hour 30 minutes
away by car.
Flights between Manila and Laoag are reported to operate daily. Check the timetable.

The church and tower are about 1–1.5 km from central Vigan. Walk or take a tricycle to Bantay. A short ride within Vigan and a ride across the town boundary can cost different amounts, so agree on the destination and total fare first.
For a horse carriage, confirm a Bantay stop, waiting time and the total first. Vigan’s heritage travel guide gives
per hour as a city example.
It is within walking distance, but a ride is recommended in the midday heat.
Bantay has the same tropical savanna climate as Vigan, with a dry season from about November to April and a wet season from May to October. The average temperature is about
. The area around the church and the hill is outdoors, so plan your day to avoid midday heat and rainy-season showers.

Vigan and its surroundings are reported to be hit by 7 to 10 typhoons a year, so check the forecast from August to October. Around the feast of Saint Augustine in early May you can see town events, but confirm the date locally.

rows: Visit early morning or late afternoon; town festival in early May
Check the forecast; stay mostly inside the church on rainy days

The easiest way is to stay in Vigan's old town and visit Bantay as a day trip. Wikivoyage lists Vigan Hotel at about ₱500 for a double, Casa Teofila Lodge at about ₱1,079–1,476, Villa Angela Heritage House at about ₱1,500–2,800 and El Juliana Hotel at about ₱1,500. Prices change with the season, so check when you book.
Typical food includes Vigan empanada, sinanglao, arroz caldo, miki and okoy. Wikivoyage lists Insiang's Empanada (
) and First Sinanglaoan (
). Vigan longganisa is spicy, unlike the Pampanga version. A visit to Bantay takes only half a day, so it is easy to return to Vigan for meals.
The church is a place of worship. Enter quietly, with shoulders and knees covered.
The grounds and the tower stairs have separate access conditions. A 2026 guide describes viewing the tower from the grounds and advises checking stair access with the caretaker.
Refrain from photography during Mass, and check the schedule locally.
Agree on the fare and waiting time for the tricycle in advance; asking for a round trip is easier.
There is little shade at midday, so bring a hat, water and sunscreen.
The Saint Augustine festival may be held in early May, and it may be crowded.
It is convenient to combine this with Vigan's old town: Bantay in the morning and the old town in the afternoon.
The church and tower are in one compound, so visit them on the same day, and it is safer not to plan to climb inside the tower.
Part of the bell tower collapsed in the 2022 earthquake. Never enter areas where access is restricted.
Restoration status and opening hours change often, so the information in this guide is for reference.
Avoid loud voices and flash photography inside the church.
Tricycle and kalesa fares are negotiated, so settle the price first.
During typhoon season (August–October), plans can change, so leave some slack.
Do not lean on or climb old brick walls and structures cracked by the earthquake.
The old town of the UNESCO World Heritage city of
Vigan
is right next door. You can walk to the cathedral, the museums and Calle Crisologo.
Vigan's central square, with a 17th-century obelisk and an evening dancing fountain. It is a good light stop after visiting Bantay.
A signature street food of Vigan.
Vigan empanada
makes a good snack after the church visit.
Heading north, you reach
Paoay Church
in Ilocos Norte. Confirm the travel time locally.
